children: Gold futures slip in rangebound trade as the market awaits Wednesday's U.S. consumer price inflation data and its implications for Fed interest-rate policy. "Expectations of an October Fed rate hike remained subdued ahead of U.S. economic data this week, but markets are still pricing in a strong chance of a hike in December," Critical Metals CEO Tony Sage says in a note. "This could keep gold at risk." Softer CPI or PPI numbers this week could help gold rebound, but "stronger-than-expected prints may lift the dollar and yields, pushing the yellow metal lower," he adds. Front-month gold for October delivery settles down 0.3% at $4,152.90 a troy ounce. Silver falls 1.6% to $59.161 a troy ounce. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
